clue.text: Grey-haired duke's accumulated wealth

parts.note: hoar means grey or white with age, as in hoary hair
D is the standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: An elderly silver-haired nobleman has piled up a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden stockpile of money or treasure, which is wealth that has been accumulated.

clue.text: Drunk comes down to earth in mountainous region

parts.note: high means intoxicated
an aircraft that lands comes down to the ground

explanation.surface: A tipsy traveller touches down in hill country.
explanation.walkthrough: THE HIGHLANDS is the mountainous north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlands are a high, hilly area, which is a mountainous region.

clue.text: Foreigner given a right of possession

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: An outsider is granted a legal claim to property.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a citizen of another country, so a foreigner.

clue.text: Hung about and longed to embrace everyone

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the word for longed wraps round the other

parts.note: died means longed, as in dying to do something
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Someone loitered, aching to hug the whole crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to dawdle or linger, so dallied means hung about.

clue.text: Thumping son, husband leaves complaining peevishly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

indicators.note: the husband leaves, so his letter is dropped from the complaining word

parts.note: whingeing is moaning in a peevish way

explanation.surface: A hard-hitting boy, whose father walks out, keeps moaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumping' looks like hitting but is the adjective meaning huge. Swingeing is mainly British, said of severe cuts or fines.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingeing means severe or crushing, as a thumping great blow or a thumping fine would be.

clue.text: Express amusement about current comparison

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for showing amusement goes round

parts.note: to smile is to show amusement
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone grins about an up-to-date comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another with like or as.

clue.text: Person engaged at home to look after journalist

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to look after
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A fiance stays in to care for a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Your intended is the person you are engaged to marry.

clue.text: One who has beef and game bird on river

parts.note: the grouse is a game bird

explanation.surface: A diner with beef and game birds sits by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat but means a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouser is a grumbler, someone with a beef, which is slang for a complaint.

clue.text: Not a clue I devised for "treat with vaccine'!

indicators.note: devised means invented, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter insists the clue is not their own invention.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to give someone a vaccine to protect against disease.

clue.text: Show embarrassment, being transfixed

definitions.meaning: to blush, read as two words: to turn crimson
pierced right through, as by a bull's horn

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word means turn crimson with shame; whole, it means pierced by horns, as one is transfixed.

clue.text: Cunning cat going back round lake for bird

indicators.note: the cunning and the backward cat go round the lake abbreviation

parts.note: guile is crafty cunning
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

indicators.note: going back says the word for the cat is written from right to left

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A sly feline circles a lake in pursuit of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is the male cat, not any feline; the lake abbreviation sits inside the cunning word, not between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Ostrogoth leader's grim reputation

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: dour means stern and grim

explanation.surface: A Gothic chieftain has a fearsome name.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the phrase 'in good odour', meaning well thought of.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean standing or esteem, as in being in bad odour with someone.

clue.text: Man possibly beset by protracted noise in channel

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on both sides, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: protracted means long-drawn-out
a sound is a noise
the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: Someone is plagued by a prolonged racket while in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Island Sound is the tidal strait between Long Island and Connecticut, a channel of the Atlantic.

clue.text: Eg Pooter's reason for not bringing murder charge?

definitions.meaning: Charles Pooter is the self-important clerk in The Diary of a ..., so he is an example of an insignificant person; the 's stands for is

definitions.text: reason for not bringing murder charge?
definitions.meaning: without a corpse a murder case is hard to bring

explanation.surface: A fictional diarist is the reason a murder prosecution falls through.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooter is the hero of the Grossmiths' comic novel The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is an unimportant person, and split in two the word says there is no corpse.

clue.text: Performers may succeed in jumping on this

definitions.text: Performers may succeed in jumping on this

parts.words: Performers may succeed in jumping on this
parts.note: reads as acrobats leaping onto a vehicle, but means people joining a popular cause to share its success; performers are also a band

explanation.definitionFit: To jump on the bandwagon is to join a trend in hope of success; originally a wagon carrying a band.

clue.text: Nobleman in swindle gets the red light

indicators.note: in places the nobleman within the swindle

parts.note: ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A lord caught in a scam gets the warning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear lamp is the red light at the back of a vehicle.

clue.text: Dogmatic sailor leaves hire vehicle, eager to go inside

indicators.note: inside says the eager word goes within what remains
the sailor leaves, so his letters drop out of the vehicle

parts.note: a pedicab is a pedal-powered taxi for hire
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
agog means eagerly expectant

explanation.surface: A rigid sailor quits a hired cab, impatient to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: A pedicab is a cycle rickshaw. 'Dogmatic' looks like the start of an anagram with 'Dog', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedagogic, of teaching, can mean schoolmasterly and dogmatic in manner.

clue.text: Cavalrymen sound like staunch colleagues

indicators.note: sound like says what follows is the same when spoken

parts.note: troupers are reliable, loyal workers who keep going

explanation.surface: Mounted soldiers seem to be loyal comrades.
explanation.definitionFit: Troopers are soldiers in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Cushy job at home in protected environment

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the protected word surrounds the other

parts.note: secure means protected
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: An easy post is one with safe surroundings at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little or no work, the very model of a cushy job.

clue.text: Nasal inflammation starts to attack a bishop in church

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces within the church abbreviation

parts.note: the starting letters of the word attack
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A sniffle begins as an assault on a bishop in a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to attack' takes the first two letters, not one; RR, Right Reverend, is the bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is inflammation of mucous membranes, especially in the nose, with excess mucus.

clue.text: An excessive desire? I'll go along with that

parts.note: an gives the letter A
greed is excessive desire for more

explanation.surface: Someone admits to wanting too much and is told they have a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying agreed is how one consents to a proposal, the same as saying one will go along with it.

clue.text: Farms found where one river flows into another

indicators.note: flows into puts one piece inside another

parts.note: the Ganges is another river, in India
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Farmland lies at a confluence of two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one river' is R and 'another' the GANGES; R goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a farm with its buildings, often a country house.

clue.text: Old German secret police's lack of activity

parts.note: the Stasi were the secret police of the former East Germany
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.surface: The East German secret service had gone inactive.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's, usually ignored, here gives its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of stagnation where nothing changes or moves.

clue.text: Stand to reason, but fail to utter on leaving

definitions.meaning: to stand to reason is to be obvious without needing to be said
read literally, to depart without saying anything such as goodbye

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense takes the phrase literally: to go off without saying a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be so obvious that it need not be stated, just as something that stands to reason.

clue.text: Inform on someone providing marijuana

definitions.meaning: British slang for informing to the police

explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang senses: betraying a person to the police, and the drug cannabis.

clue.text: Man grasping woman's characteristic style

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so the Man abbreviation goes round

parts.note: IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A man holds on to a lady's distinctive manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic mode of expression, as in the jazz idiom.

clue.text: Boring instrument a soothsayer heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for the soothsayer is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: an augur was a Roman prophet who read omens

explanation.surface: A dull tool overheard a fortune-teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull' but means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a drilling tool for making holes, so it is used for boring.

clue.text: Gradually moving round unknown turn, relaxed

indicators.note: round says the moving word is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: easing means moving slowly and carefully
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Inching around an unseen corner, a driver stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the easing word round both the unknown and the turn, not round one alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going describes a laid-back person, one who is relaxed and tolerant.

clue.text: Result of combining shy sets in new constitution

indicators.note: a new constitution makes up the letters in a fresh way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bashful groups end up under a newly drafted charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new constitution' rearranges SHY, SETS and IN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthesis is a whole made by combining separate elements.

clue.text: Shrub French writer rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the writer's name is written backwards

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French novelist and philosopher

explanation.surface: A bush was spurned by a novelist from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree whose berries give a tart spice.
